one_month_reasoning: NXP investor relations confirms two scheduled events in the window (supervisor fact-check). Q3 2026 results come out on 2026-10-27 at 4:10 PM ET (guide $3.75B revenue, $4.11 non-GAAP EPS), so the first reaction is on Oct 28. The FOMC decision is at 2:00 PM ET on Oct 28, after the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16. TXN and STM report the week before, a read-across for sector sentiment. The last two earnings weeks moved +21% and -15%, so the sign of the print reaction is close to a coin flip. I treat Polymarket's ~67% October-hike odds (secondary relay) as sentiment only: a hike is largely expected. I use a near-symmetric mixture centred at ~$237.5, 85% at a 12% monthly sigma and 15% at 21%, for an effective ~13.3%. That is slightly wider than round 1 because realized volatility is 45-47% even outside earnings weeks. The long-run monthly volatility since 2011 is only ~36% annualized (~10.5% a month), but an earnings gap falls inside this window, so I stay near the 47%/3.5 = 13.4% rule.

fair_value.method: A 0.6/0.4 blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of ~$19.4 x 14x = $272) and FCF yield (2027E FCF $3.6B at a 5.5% yield on ~252M shares = $259), giving ~$267.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS as of Sep-2027 ~$19.4 (2027 consensus $18.10 rolled forward 3 quarters to ~$19.8, haircut ~2% for cycle and consensus drift) x 14.0x forward P/E

inputs_detail.value: $18.10 (range $16.26-$20.38, 26 analysts; 17 upward revisions in 30 days per the supervisor's check)

inputs_detail.derivation: I roll 2027 consensus of $18.10 forward three quarters at the low end of management's 6-10% revenue CAGR, with operating leverage, to get ~$19.8. I cut the round-1 cycle haircut from ~4% to ~2% because revisions are currently running up (17 raises in 30 days), not down. I keep some haircut because China revenue (+25.5% y/y) is outrunning China car retail (-20.8% YTD) and channel inventory is 11 weeks against 9 a year ago.

NXP's typical forward range is 14-18x, and it trades at ~13.1x 2027 EPS now. The 10-year median trailing P/E is ~24x, which is ~16x forward in normal-growth years. I stay at the low end because the Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 (confirmed by the Fed) caps re-rating. My first-hike base rate (below) says hikes in an expansion have not usually derailed analog semis, so I do not go below 14x.
2027 revenue is ~$15.9B: 2026E $14.24B plus management's 'double-digit growth in 2027', trimmed to ~11.5%. I apply a ~23% FCF margin, which is Q2's 22.6% (791/3496) plus modest leverage.
The current TTM FCF yield is 4.7% ($2.81B / $59.6B market cap). NXP's historical range is 4.5-6.5%. I use the middle of that range because the Fed is hiking.
Already reflected, since FCF is after interest (equity FCF).

bear.story: The cycle rolls over. China auto-related orders prove to have been pull-ins (NXP China revenue is +25.5% y/y while CPCA retail is -20.8% YTD), channel inventory builds past 11 weeks, and the Fed keeps hiking. 2027 EPS is cut to ~$15 and the multiple sits at 11x. That echoes 2022, when NXPI fell ~21% within six months of the first hike (Mar-2022 $185 to Sep-2022 $148) even though EPS grew.

base.story: The upcycle continues and revisions stay positive. 2027 EPS lands near $18 with NTM ~$19 at the horizon, and the forward multiple holds ~13.5-14x. That is consistent with the base rate that analog semis finished the 12 months after a first Fed hike higher in 7 of 8 cases (TXN, ADI and NXPI across 2004, 2015 and 2022).

bull.story: Management delivers double-digit 2027 growth and ~60% gross margin, and EPS estimates rise toward $20. Auto and industrial content plus pricing re-rate the stock to ~17x, back to the May 2026 high of ~$340.

thesis_break_reason: Below the $183 52-week low and ~9.7x the $18.10 2027 consensus. A trade there would most likely mean the upcycle has broken: a China or channel inventory unwind (channel inventory is already 11 weeks against 9, and China retail is -21% YTD), a pricing reversal, or a rate-driven downturn. Plain volatility is less likely at that level. Moves between $200 and $230 are ordinary for a stock with 47% realized volatility. NXPI has spent little time below ~$180 since 2023, except the April 2025 tariff panic.

key_uncertainties: Whether the Fed hiking cycle (3.75-4.00% after Sep 16, more projected) ends the upturn. The history says it usually does not within 12 months, but it causes deep drawdowns along the way (2022).
China pull-in risk: NXP China revenue is +25.5% y/y against China car retail -20.8% YTD. China is only ~18% of revenue, but channel inventory is up to 11 weeks.
The durability of auto semis demand and pricing (auto is ~55% of revenue)
Volatility regime: 47% realized now against ~29% 12-month log-return dispersion historically. It is unclear how much of today's volatility persists over a year.
Section 232 tariff phase 2, and whether the Ambarella talks turn into a deal
reasoning: In round 2 I re-derived the width and the rate-cycle base rate, as the supervisor asked. (1) First-hike base rate, from Twelve Data monthly closes, month-end of the first hike to 12 months later. TXN: Jun-2004 +16%, Dec-2015 +33%, Mar-2022 +1%. ADI: Jun-2004 -21%, Dec-2015 +31%, Mar-2022 +19%. NXPI: Dec-2015 +16%, Mar-2022 +1%. That is 7 of 8 up, with a median of ~+16%. So my round-1 claim that hiking into an upcycle 'precedes analog tops' holds for intra-year drawdowns (NXPI fell -20% by Sep-2022, and 2018 was a mid-cycle top), but not for 12-month outcomes. That weakens my bearish tilt, and I raise the median slightly, from ~$248 to ~$251. (2) Width. The supervisor measured 47% weekly realized volatility over 52 weeks and 45% over 13 weeks. My own NXPI history shows 12-month log returns with a standard deviation of 0.29 over 2011-2026 and 0.23 over 2021-2026, and monthly-annualized volatility of 35-37%. Twelve-month outcomes mean-revert relative to short-horizon volatility. I therefore disagree with widening all the way to 45%, but I accept that 36% was too narrow for the current regime. I now use an 85/15 mixture of lognormals (sigma 0.38 and 0.56, medians $251 and $245), which implies an effective ~41% sigma between K=142 and K=355. The five-year history supports a right tail no fatter than P(>=+35%) ~0.2-0.3 (16% of windows since 2021 and 23% since 2016), and my P(>=319) is 0.27. (3) Facts. 2027 consensus is $18.10 with revisions running up, so I cut my EPS drift haircut from 4% to 2% and fair value rises from $263 to $267. China divergence and channel inventory are real but bounded (18% of revenue), which keeps the bear case at 25%. I downgrade the Polymarket odds to sentiment: they no longer move any number, and the confirmed Fed hike does the work. The DRAM claim and the Ambarella deal do not enter my numbers. The scenario mean is ~$257, and the ladder median is ~$251, below fair value because of the left-skew risk from the China and channel data. No option data was consulted.
